Restated before interest: REGN paid $167mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 0.40% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 9.20% to 8.79%. Restated at replacement capex: REGN spent $2,373mm on plant over 2023 to 2025 against $1,048mm of depreciation and amortisation less amortisation of intangibles, 3.18% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 8.79% to 5.24%. Restated without one-off cash: REGN's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $411mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately. None recurs, so the charge falls from 5.24% to 4.25%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 REGN's cash flow statement shows receivables up $395mm, inventories up $1,167mm, payables and accrued liabilities up $2,070mm, a working capital release of $509mm, 1.22% of revenue. A release flatters the window once and does not recur, so the charge rises from 4.25% to 5.62%. Rebuilt on the book's own ratios on 0.4039 of the revenue they are struck on, against 0.3477 the filings leave as cash over 2023 to 2025 (free cash flow before interest, at replacement capex, without one-off cash and without working capital build), so the charge is 5.6184%.
